ip_top_stories.title: Nvidia hit with US copyright suit claiming it trained AI models on Winamp subsidiary Jamendo's music without permission
ip_top_stories.summary: Music licensing platform Jamendo has filed a US copyright lawsuit against Nvidia, alleging the company used Jamendo's catalogue of licensed music to train its AI models without authorisation. The suit describes the alleged use as 'a blatant violation' of copyright. A separate but related article from Billboard covers the same filing.

ip_top_stories.title: Eleonora Rosati, lawyer: 'Artists are already thinking about how to protect themselves from AI; Taylor Swift has registered her voice'
ip_top_stories.summary: IP lawyer Eleonora Rosati discusses how artists, including Taylor Swift, are taking proactive steps to protect their identities and creative output from AI exploitation, including registering their voices. The interview covers the broader legal landscape around AI and copyright protection for creators.

ip_top_stories.title: 'We will not stand for it': Coalition warns of 'fight' over any Labor plan to allow an AI copyright law carve-out
ip_top_stories.summary: Australia's Coalition opposition has warned it will strongly resist any move by the Labor government to introduce an AI copyright exception, with rights holders and creative industries also signalling fierce opposition. The dispute follows reports of a top-secret government AI copyright proposal that has drawn criticism from senators.

ip_top_stories.title: Getty opens its archive to ChatGPT as OpenAI deal sends shares soaring
ip_top_stories.summary: Getty Images has struck a licensing deal with OpenAI, granting ChatGPT access to its extensive photo archive. The announcement sent Getty's shares sharply higher and marks one of the more significant content licensing agreements between a major image rights holder and an AI company.

ip_top_stories.title: Artist-Led Udio and Suno Copyright Lawsuits Add New Law Firm
ip_top_stories.summary: The copyright lawsuits brought by artists against AI music generation platforms Udio and Suno have gained additional legal representation, with a new law firm joining the cases. The litigation, which centres on alleged unauthorised use of copyrighted music in AI training, continues to develop.

ip_further_links.title: Nvidia Seeks To Toss 3D Artist's 'Copycat' Copyright AI Suit
ip_further_links.summary: Nvidia has moved to dismiss a copyright infringement lawsuit filed by a 3D artist who alleged the company's AI system copied their work.

ip_further_links.title: Inside AIMP 2026: Glen Ballard and U.S. Copyright Office Leaders Debate A.I., Ownership, and the Future of Music Publishing
ip_further_links.summary: At the AIMP 2026 conference, music industry figures and US Copyright Office leaders debated AI's impact on ownership and the future of music publishing rights.

ip_further_links.title: New Law Would Give Artists Sweeping Protections Against AI Stealing Their Work
ip_further_links.summary: A proposed new law in the US would introduce broad protections for artists against AI systems using their work without consent or compensation.

ip_further_links.title: APRA AMCOS Reveals Australian And New Zealand Songs Found In AI Training Datasets
ip_further_links.summary: Australian and New Zealand music rights body APRA AMCOS has disclosed that songs from its members have been identified in datasets used to train AI models.

ip_further_links.title: SOCAN Responds to Canada's New AI Strategy, Calls to Protect Copyrighted Music
ip_further_links.summary: Canadian music rights organisation SOCAN has responded to Canada's new AI strategy, calling on the government to ensure stronger protections for copyrighted music in the context of AI development.

ip_further_links.title: Big Tech Is a Thief and a Liar, Says New York Times Publisher
ip_further_links.summary: The publisher of the New York Times has publicly accused Big Tech companies of theft and dishonesty in relation to the use of journalism to train AI models, in the context of the newspaper's ongoing litigation against OpenAI.

ip_further_links.title: Guest Post — Legitimate but Not Loved: What Academic Librarians Think About AI
ip_further_links.summary: A guest post on The Scholarly Kitchen explores survey findings on academic librarians' attitudes toward AI tools — broadly accepting their legitimacy but expressing significant reservations.

ip_further_links.title: Vietnam's publishers seek stronger copyright protections in AI era
ip_further_links.summary: Vietnamese publishers are calling for enhanced copyright protections in response to the growing use of their content in AI training and generation.

ip_further_links.title: Senior Albanese minister clashes with Pocock over top-secret AI copyright claim
ip_further_links.summary: An Australian government minister has clashed with Senator Pocock in parliament over allegations that a government AI copyright proposal is being kept secret from lawmakers and the public.

ip_further_links.title: Unauthorised fashion upcycling held unlawful by French first instance court
ip_further_links.summary: A French court has ruled that the unauthorised upcycling of branded fashion items infringes intellectual property rights, in a decision with potential implications for the boundaries of IP protection.
